title: Interview prep
blurb: Daily practice for PhD research scientist and applied scientist loops: coding rounds, ML fundamentals, and building a transformer from scratch.

tracks.title: Coding interviews
tracks.blurb: LeetCode-style problems grouped by pattern. Aim for a clean solution with the right complexity in 25 to 35 minutes, talking through it the way you would on a call.

modules.title: Arrays, hashing, two pointers, sliding window

tracks.title: ML fundamentals
tracks.blurb: Implement the core algorithms from scratch in NumPy, the way ML coding rounds ask for them, and be able to explain every design choice.

tracks.title: Build a transformer
tracks.blurb: From a byte-pair tokenizer to a trained GPT, one piece at a time. NumPy for the mechanics, PyTorch for training.

tracks.title: ML system and research design
tracks.blurb: Open-ended prompts scored against a rubric. Write or talk through the answer in 30 minutes, then grade yourself or have Claude grade it.
